threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at the bus stops when it says 'Due' instead of a specific time. We all figured that out the first week.
Caught a night bus and the driver stopped for a local cat trying to cross the road. Everyone cheered. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy serenading his cat on a balcony while a busker played behind him. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar with a dance floor made entirely of recycled skateboards. It’s as quirky as the crowd it draws.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they argue about the best taco truck without mentioning La Taqueria—classic tourist mistake.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watching the 31BX roll up at 5:01 PM every weekday feels like witnessing a magic trick: packed one moment, empty the next, as if all the commuters vanished.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all the quirky little shops are overpriced, but many locals find hidden gems that sell vintage clothes for next to nothing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the metro map; locals just glide right by, while newcomers are still trying to decode the lines.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for a bus schedule but just get a shrug and a 'it'll come when it comes.' Didn’t know patience was a local rule.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week. Guy next to me was trying to start a karaoke session. Apparently, he thinks he sounds like Adele. He didn't.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really in Neukölln when I saw a guy in a full tuxedo ordering döner at 3 AM while a street musician played an accordion nearby.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it's normal to see a group of punks setting up a pop-up bar in an abandoned building on a Saturday night. Just grab a drink and join the party.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays—no panic, just a resigned sigh and a text to friends about the latest train drama.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a sequined suit serenading commuters at the Civic Center station while a rat scuttled past. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the fireworks are just for festivals—try telling them it's locals celebrating a weekend's end at 3 AM. Sleep? Not in Gràcia.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for 'café con leche' instead of just 'café'—classic sign they're not yet in tune with the locals.
